registration.trigger: paying wages over $100 in any calendar quarter

efile.text: All employers must electronically submit employment tax returns, wage reports, and payroll tax deposits to the Employment Development Department (EDD).

epay.text: All employers must electronically submit payroll tax deposits to EDD.

deposits.interpretation: California's deposit schedule for State Disability Insurance (SDI) and Personal Income Tax (PIT) withholding follows the employer's federal deposit schedule and the California PIT accumulated. Bands: under $350, $350 to $400 inclusive, over $400. Rows (DE 44 p.5, p.60): federal next-day: over $400 next-day, $350-$400 monthly, under $350 quarterly; federal semiweekly: over $400 semiweekly, $350-$400 monthly, under $350 quarterly; federal monthly/quarterly/annual: $350 or more monthly, under $350 quarterly. INTERPRETATION: the guide says 'accumulate ... during one or more payroll periods' without defining the accumulation window, so each FEDERAL deposit group (a semiweekly period, a next-day group, or a calendar month for monthly federal depositors) is banded on the PIT withheld in it; a group in the $350-$400 band or a federal-monthly month at $350 or more is deposited monthly (the 15th of the next month); the rest is quarterly. Employer UI and ETT are paid quarterly with the quarterly payment (the guide says they may be paid earlier).

returns.name: Quarterly Contribution Return and Report of Wages (DE 9) and Continuation (DE 9C)
contents: DE 9 reconciles the tax and withholding amounts with the DE 88 deposits for the quarter.
DE 9C reports total subject wages, personal income tax (PIT) wages and PIT withheld for each employee for the quarter.
Must be submitted even if there is no payroll during the quarter.

notModelled: The DE 9 line-by-line form layout and the wage-report file format were not read.
Employment Training Tax (0.1% on the first $7,000, DE 44 p.8) is not emitted as a separate line by the paycheck engine, so it is not in these totals.

EDD's 2026 table lists February 17 both as Lunar New Year (next business day February 18) and as the next business day after Presidents' Day (February 16). The two cannot both hold, so February 17 is left out of the holiday dates: a due date on February 16 resolves to February 17 as printed, and one on February 17 resolves to February 17, one day earlier than the table's February 18 (the safe direction).
